steps.body: When a line (a **transversal**) crosses two **parallel** lines, it makes eight angles — but only two different sizes. **Corresponding angles** (same position at each crossing) are equal, and **alternate interior angles** (opposite sides, between the lines) are equal too.

widget.prompt: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. One angle is 70°. What is its corresponding angle at the other crossing?

commonErrors.feedback: That's the SUPPLEMENT — corresponding angles are EQUAL, so it's 70°, not 110°.
Corresponding angles are equal, not complementary — it's 70°.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Corresponding angles at parallel-line crossings are equal, so it's also 70°.

steps.body: Angles that sit together on a straight line are **supplementary** — they add to 180°. So next to a 70° angle, the angle completing the straight line is 110°. Co-interior angles (same side, between the lines) are supplementary this way.

explanationVariants: Angles on a straight line add to 180°, so the partner of 70° is 180 − 70 = 110°.

widget.prompt: Two angles sit together on a straight line. One is 70°. What is the other?

commonErrors.feedback: Those would be EQUAL — angles on a straight line are SUPPLEMENTARY: 180 − 70 = 110°.
That's the complement (to 90°) — on a straight LINE they add to 180°: 180 − 70 = 110°.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Angles on a straight line add to 180°: 180 − 70 = 110°.

explanationVariants: Alternate interior angles at parallel lines are equal, so it matches: 65°.
Alternate interior angles are equal across a transversal: 65°.

widget.prompt: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. An interior angle is 65°. What is its alternate interior angle?

commonErrors.feedback: Alternate interior angles are EQUAL, not supplementary — it's 65°, not 115°.
Alternate interior angles are equal, not complementary — it's 65°.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Alternate interior angles at parallel lines are equal, so it's also 65°.

widget.prompt: Two angles are in the SAME position at each of the two crossings (e.g., both top-right). What are they called?

options.label: Corresponding angles — they're equal
options.feedback: Right — same-position angles are corresponding, and they're equal at parallel lines.

options.label: Supplementary angles — they add to 180°
options.feedback: Same-position (corresponding) angles are EQUAL, not supplementary.

options.label: Complementary angles — they add to 90°
options.feedback: Corresponding angles are equal, not complementary.

options.label: Vertical angles
options.feedback: Vertical angles share a single vertex; same-position angles at DIFFERENT crossings are corresponding.

explanationVariants: The corresponding angle of 120° is 120°; the angle next to it on the line is 180 − 120 = 60°.

widget.prompt: An angle is 120°. On a straight line next to its corresponding angle, what is the remaining angle?

commonErrors.feedback: The corresponding angle is 120°, but its straight-line PARTNER is 180 − 120 = 60°.
Angles on a line add to 180°, not 360° — 180 − 120 = 60°.

widget.fallbackFeedback: The corresponding angle is 120°, and its supplement is 180 − 120 = 60°.

steps.body: Match transversal angle pairs to their rule.
explanationVariants: Corresponding and alternate interior angles are EQUAL; co-interior (same-side interior) angles are SUPPLEMENTARY (sum 180°).
Equal: corresponding, alternate interior. Supplementary: co-interior.

widget.prompt: Match each angle pair at parallel lines to its relationship.

pairErrors.feedback: Co-interior (same-side interior) angles are SUPPLEMENTARY (add to 180°), not equal.

widget.missFeedback: Not quite — corresponding and alternate interior are equal; co-interior angles add to 180°.
widget.successFeedback: Right — same-side interior angles are the supplementary pair; the others are equal.

hints: Alternate interior angles (opposite sides, between the lines) are also equal.
Co-interior angles (same side, between the lines) are supplementary — they add to 180°.

steps.body: A transversal across parallel lines makes equal and supplementary angle pairs.
takeaways: Corresponding and alternate interior angles are equal.
Angles on a straight line (and co-interior angles) add to 180°.
Chaining these rules finds any of the eight angles.
